facts.text: Branch was originally to be named Turner after the first postmaster, but the name changed because another Branch post office existed in Phillips County.
Branch grew into a coal mining community along the Arkansas Central Railroad, which arrived in 1898 and linked the area to larger western Arkansas centers.
The town's precise geographic coordinates are 35°18′20″N 93°57′13″W, with an average elevation of 466 feet (142 meters) above sea level.
The town experiences a humid subtropical climate typical of the region, characterized by hot summers and mild winters.
The settlement evolved from earlier pioneer routes including the old Military Road used during the Indian removal era of the 1830s.
